title: Optimization of AAV9 Dose and Fluorescein Concentration for Vagus Nerve Injection in Rats
content: Background/Objectives: Direct intraneural delivery of adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) via peripheral nerves remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated the feasibility of AAV9 delivery into the vagus nerve, identified an optimal dose, and determined an optimal fluorescein dye concentration for tracking injection fidelity. Methods: Rats received left vagus nerve injections of 5 µL AAV9/GFP at doses of 2.5 × 10⁹, 2.5 × 10¹⁰, 7.6 × 10¹⁰, 2.5 × 10¹¹, or 6.5 × 10¹¹ vector genomes (vg)/rat, mixed with 1% luxol fast blue dye. Controls received vehicle with dye. Transduction in the nodose ganglia of the vagus nerve and medulla was assessed. Fluorescein compatibility was evaluated in CHO Lec2 cells using concentrations of 0%, 0.0001%, 0.004%, and 0.01% at high and low multiplicities of infection. In vivo compatibility was subsequently confirmed using 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat with 0.001%, 0.002%, 0.004%, or 0.008% fluorescein. Results: Transduction of critical autonomic nervous system sites increased with dose. The two highest doses (2.5 × 10¹¹ and 6.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat) produced abundant, comparable transduction in the nodose ganglia and medulla, identifying 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat as the optimal dose. Fluorescein did not inhibit AAV9 transduction in CHO Lec2 cells at the concentrations tested. In vivo, 0.004% fluorescein provided clear visualization during vagus nerve injection. Conclusions: Direct intraneural administration of AAV9/GFP at 2.5 × 10¹¹ vg/rat with 0.004% fluorescein offers an effective formulation for vagus nerve delivery in rats. Further validation and dose-scaling studies are suggested to establish feasibility for translation to larger animals and humans.
